Dr. Pawaton Kaemawichanurat is an Associate Professor of Mathematics in the Department of Mathematics at King Mongkut's University of Technology Thonburi (KMUTT) in Bangkok, Thailand. He holds a B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Mathematics from Silpakorn University and earned his Ph.D. in Mathematics from Curtin University, Australia. His research interests lie primarily in graph theory (including domination and Hamiltonian properties of graphs), combinatorics, and topics in computational geometry. He has co-authored multiple research publications in areas such as domination in graphs, semipaired domination, and connected domination critical graphs, and he participates in academic committees and conference organization in mathematics.</p>

             <div class="left_title_border mb-2">
                <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>About Conference</h3> 
             </div>
             <p><strong>The International Conference on “Statistical Theory and Applications for Trends” (STAT-2025) aims to become the leading 
             annual conference in the fields related to Statistical research and its applications. </strong></p>
             <p>The goal of this statistics conference 
             is to gather scholars from all over the world to present advances in the relevant fields and to foster an environment conducive 
             to exchanging ideas and information. It also provides the premier and multi-disciplinary forum for researchers, practitioners 
             and educators to present and discuss the most recent developments, trends and concerns practical challenges encountered and 
             the solution adopted in the field of mathematics, statistics, operations research, computations techniques, computer science. 
             This conference will also provide an ideal environment to meet experts and develop new collaborations on the fundamentals, 
             applications, and products of the mentioned fields.</p>

             <p>The STAT-2025 is a place of presenting new studies on theory and applications of statistics as well as exchanging knowledge 
             of new computational techniques. It is addressed to academic community as well as representatives of the private sector, 
             statistical offices, polling organizations and other public institutions. The conference would be studded with a Keynote Address, 
             Special Invited Lectures, Invited talks by Senior Researchers and Contributed papers session. Overall, the conference will provide 
             the researchers and attendees with prospects for national and international collaboration and networking among universities and 
             institutions from India and abroad for promoting research.</p>
            
          </article>

          <article class="pdf-viewer"> 
              
             <div class="left_title_border mb-2">
                <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>About University</h3> 
             </div>
             <p>St Joseph's University (SJU) is a Jesuit university at the heart of Bengaluru, the Silicon city of India. 
             Established in 1882 by Paris foreign Fathers, the management of the college was handed over to the Jesuit order 
             (Society of Jesus) in 1937. The college was first affiliated to the university of Madras and later to the Mysore 
             and Bangalore universities. In 1986, St Joseph's College became the first affiliated college in Karnataka to offer 
             postgraduate courses. In 1988, it became the first college in Karnataka to get a research centre and in 2005, 
             it was one of five colleges in Karnataka that was awarded academic autonomy. In February 2021, St Joseph's University 
             bill was presented in the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and was subsequently passed by the Legislative Assembly and 
             Karnataka Legislative Councill. The college received its University status on 2nd July 2022 and was inaugurated as 
             India's first public-private university by the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu on 27 September 2022.</p>
            
          </article>
          <article class="pdf-viewer"> 
              
             <div class="left_title_border mt-5 mb-2">
                <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>About Department</h3> 
             </div>
             <p>The Department of Statistics in St Joseph's College was established in 2010. The Department of Statistics is committed to 
             excellence in teaching and equipping students to become practicing Statisticians. The department offers Undergraduate (UG) 
             and Postgraduate (PG) programs in Statistics and provides a platform for analyzing real-life data, draw conclusions, and 
             developing reasoning skills. The department also offers two certificate courses namely “Statistics using R and MS Python” 
             and “Data Science and Analytics”, along with internships and projects involving real-life data analysis. The department has 
             distinguished alumni working in various reputed companies, reflecting its commitment to quality education. It aims to instill 
             scientific temper, analytical skills, and intellectual vigor among students, so that they may contribute to the needs of society. 
             Also, the department aims to provide students with life-oriented education through projects of social relevance. Over four semesters, 
             the department offers 20 papers covering advanced statistical knowledge needed for research in statistics/applied statistics. 
             These papers are designed to impart the learning of statistical methods and tools, which is expected to improve students' 
             ability to analyses various types of real-life data.</p>
            
          </article>

        <div class="content">
          
			<div class="text-center mb-5">
      <h2 class="fw-bold">Centre for  <span class="fw-bold text-warning mb-3">Indian Knowledge System [IKS]</span></h2>
      <h5 class="text-muted mx-auto" style="max-width: 720px;">
       St Joseph's University, Bengaluru – 560 027
      </h5>
    </div>
			
			<p>Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) represent the vast and diverse intellectual traditions of India, nurtured and refined over thousands of years. Rooted in holistic thinking and experiential wisdom, IKS cover a wide spectrum of disciplines including philosophy, languages, literature, mathematics, astronomy, metallurgy, architecture, agriculture, governance, medicine (Ayurveda, Siddha, Yoga), performing arts and environmental management. These systems evolved through close observation of nature, community practices, and intergenerational knowledge transfer, making them deeply sustainable and culturally relevant.</p>

<p>Recognizing the importance of this heritage, the Government of India and the University Grants Commission (UGC) have emphasized the need to integrate IKS into higher education. The aim is not only to preserve and document traditional knowledge but also to contextualize its relevance in addressing modern challenges such as climate change, health and well-being, resource management, and social cohesion. By blending ancient insights with contemporary scientific approaches, IKS provide a unique framework for innovation, critical inquiry, and nation-building.</p>

<p>In the current academic landscape, IKS is envisioned as a platform for multidisciplinary learning. It encourages students and researchers to explore indigenous perspectives, engage with local communities, and develop solutions rooted in cultural ethos while being globally relevant. Through teaching, research, training, and outreach, IKS initiatives seek to bridge the gap between tradition and modernity, thereby fostering pride in India's intellectual heritage and contributing to sustainable development in the 21st century.</p>
			
        </div>

      </div>
    </div>

         </div>
        <p>All cadets report in their A1 uniforms. Theory classes by ANO Lt. Akshay D Mandlik along with drill and physicals taught by two PI Staff. 
        Theory classes are conducted by the ANO, which spans across topics of National integration, Aims and Objectives of NCC, etc.</p>

         <p>After the theory class, all cadets sing the NCC song, sing the National Anthem, and then are dispersed with the command of Visarjan. 
         They are directed towards the University's canteen for lunch. Food is initially served at the Martyr's Table, following the classic food tradition of 1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC TP-3.</p>
    </div>
    <div> 
         <div class="left_title_border mt-5 mb-2">
                <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> Fallins</h3> 
         </div>
        <p>We have Fallins on a daily basis in the mornings. The Fallins are focused on physicals and drill. In physicals cadets are encouraged to run, take push-ups, take crunches, etc. 
        In drill they are taught discipline and uniformity along with the basics. Theory classes are also taken regularly to brush up the various topics under B Certificate and C Certificate exams.</p>

                       qualities from all walks of life, who will serve the Nation regardless of which career they choose. Needless to say, NCC also provides an environment

         <article class="mb-5 ncc-history">

            <div class="timeline-history">
               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC is the oldest and the only Armoured squadron in Karnataka. With an exciting number of cadets, 
                   this squadron is one of the most prestigious associations of Bangalore. The root of this squadron runs deep.
                 </p>
               </div>

               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   Starting in the early 1962, the squadron has undergone many changes and much development. 
                   1 MYSORE ARMD SQN NCC was raised on 12 June 1962 and was later re-designed as 21 MYSORE ARMD NCC in December 1962. 
                   Major S.K. Dhamija of CIH was the first Commanding officer who commanded from 1st September 1962 to 14th June 1965. 
                   Again, on 17th April 1964, the squadron was re-designed as 1 MYSORE ARMD SQN NCC and further 1 MYSORE ARMD SQN NCC 
                   was re designed as 1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC on 1st November 1974.
                 </p>
               </div>

               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC was redesigned as 1 KAR (1) COY on April 2004. It was reversed back to 1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC on 14th September 2004. 
                   2/Lt Albert S was an infantry battalion officer who later attended the armed corps special course at Ahmednagar and got commissioned 
                   as ANO of 1 MYSORE ARMD SQN NCC in 1964.
                 </p>
               </div>
               
               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   In 1984 Prof Jacob Raju P was commissioned as 2nd lieutenant as ANO of 1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC of St. Joseph's College. In 1981, 
                   1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC won the Best unit award and the All India Best Cadet in RDC.
                 </p>
               </div>
               
               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   In 1997, Lt. E.M Nagrajan took over the St. Joseph's College troop and ran the office for 14 long years.
                 </p>
               </div>
               
               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   Later Prof. Akshay D Mandlik who is an alumni and Ex-NCC cadet, took over the charge of 1 KAR ARMD SQN as a Caretaker from 06/6/2011. 
                   Lt. Akshay D Mandlik underwent his NCC ANO training from January 2015 till 14th March 2015. He broke the record by winning in all the 
                   competitions he participated in and he was awarded the COMDT's silver medal from OTA Kamptee. He is the recipient of highest NCC honor Raksha Mantri Padak award.
                 </p>
               </div>
               
               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   As of June 2022, the troop strength is 56 cadets (which includes 4 vacancies of the HQ).
                 </p>
               </div>
               
               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   With its history as rich as this, the 1 KAR ARMD SQN NCC, ever since its inception in 1962 has induced more than 50 officers in the mighty 
                   Indian Army and has never failed to surprise its admirers with their achievements.
                 </p>
               </div>
               
               <div class="timeline-data">
                 <p>
                   In the academic year 2022-23 NCC became an open elective as a curriculum under the NEP policy in the University programme.
                 </p>
               </div>
               
            </div>

         </article>

                 About St Joseph's University and  <span class="text-warning">  the Department of Mathematics</span>
                </h2>
                <p class="pb-2">St Joseph's University, Bengaluru, with its 150-year Jesuit legacy, is a premier institution 
                known for academic excellence and research. It provides a dynamic learning environment that fosters critical thinking, 
                innovation, and interdisciplinary collaboration. The Department of Mathematics, established in 1923, is one of the 
                institution's oldest departments and offers undergraduate and postgraduate programs with a strong research focus.</p>

                <p>The university has a vibrant academic culture, making it an ideal venue for intellectual exchange in mathematics and its applications. </p>

               significant advancements in arithmetic formulae and circuits, with notable publications including "Partial Derivatives in Arithmetic

               applied aspects of computer science and mathematics.</p>

               His research covers a broad spectrum of mathematical areas, including the numerical solution of hyperbolic PDEs, mesh adaptation for singularly

               Fuzzy Decision Making, Soft Fuzzy Information Systems, and Octagonal Fuzzy Numbers. She has published significant work on 
               topics including finite-dimensional fuzzy normed linear spaces, the completion of fuzzy normed linear spaces, and other

               with a particular emphasis on understanding the fluid dynamics of the world's oceans. With extensive research experience, he has made

               An alumnus of the Indian Statistical Institute, Calcutta (BSc in Statistics), and the California Institute of Technology (PhD), 
               he has had a notable academic journey. Prior to joining IISc, he served as an associate professor at ISI, Bangalore, and moved 
               to IISc in 2006. He was promoted to professor at IISc in 2012. His research interests span Geometric Group Theory, Riemannian Geometry, 
               and Metric Geometry, particularly in relation to Probability Theory. He has also explored the application of topology to Molecular Biology. 
               Recently, his focus has shifted towards automated theorem proving—working on advancing the ability of computers to perform mathematical reasoning. 
               His publications include significant contributions such as his work on Gardam's disproof of Kaplansky's conjecture, "Surfaces of Infinite Type Are 
               Non-Hopfian," "Knots, Braids, and First Order Logic," and more. He has been recognized with the NASI-Scopus Young Scientist Award for his outstanding 
               contributions to the field.  </p>

               utilizing deep neural networks to analyze chaotic and periodic motions through bifurcation diagrams, Lyapunov exponents, 
               and fractal dimensions. He has published over 200 research papers in reputed international journals, including the Journal 
               of Fluid Mechanics (Cambridge University) and Physics of Fluids. He has mentored 23 Ph.D. students and collaborated with 
               researchers across the globe. Dr. Siddheshwar has received numerous accolades, including the President of India Award, 
               Young Scientist Award, Indian Mathematical Society Prize, Sir C. V. Raman Award, and the Royal Society Incoming Fellowship 
               (London). He has held visiting positions at leading institutions worldwide and has been featured in the Stanford 2% list

<section class="verification-section py-5 px-4">
  <div class="container pt-5 pb-2">

    <div class="verify-card mb-4">
      <div class="align-items-start gap-4"> 

        <div class="content">
          <h3 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3">Social Concern</h3>
          <p>Preparing persons for the services of others is the aims of educations in St Joseph's University. 
            At The heart of the University in Social Concern. Students are expected to be sensitive to the poor and be persons of concern, compassion and conscience.</p> 
        </div>

      </div>
    </div>
    
    <div class="verify-card mb-4">
      <div class="align-items-start gap-4"> 

        <div class="content">
          <h3 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3">What is Outreach?</h3>
          <p>The jesuit view of Higher education has never been a simplistic and one-sided one. It concerns all round development with a special focus on 
          critical praxis that engages students to yoke their academics excellence, their character development and their personal concern to the transformation 
          of society deeply disturbed by inequality and injustice. The students that passes through jesuit higher education cannot remain isolated from the economics, 
          political and cultural fabric of his/ her society. It is integral to higher education that he / she becomes aware of and is involved in the everyday realities 
          of society. It is the jesuit ideal that solidarity with the people can only be achieved by 'contact' and 'participation' in the daily life of the marginalized. 
          It is therefore the firm conviction of Jesuit Higher Education that 'personal involvement with innocent suffering, with the injustice other suffer, is the catalyst 
          for solidarity which then gives rise to intellectual inquiry and moral reflections'. </p>

          <p>In alignment with Jesuits Higher Education purposes, the University Grants Commission, the Higher Education Authority in India, has recognized the 
          relevance and importance of the purposes and practice to 'Extension' as integral to the process of learning. Hence it expects universities and Universitys, 
          given their knowledge, human resources and infrastructure, to become positive change – makers who would empower the marginalized of the society. </p> 
        </div>

      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="verify-card mb-4">
      <div class="align-items-start gap-4"> 

        <div class="content">
          <h3 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3">Why Outreach?</h3>
          <p>The Outreach program draws its inspiration from the University's vision of formimg women and men for others. 
          It will provide students with a platform to explore and develop the art of critical thinking, the skill of leadership 
          and techniques of meaningful interventions aimed at building a just equitable society . It further draws its roots from 
          the Brizilian educator Paulo Friere's Philosophy of Action – Reflection – Praxis.</p>

          <p>In the view of the UGC and the NAAC recommendations on Extension, the objective of the outreach programme is to extend 
          knowledge and other institutional resources to the community and vice – versa. It is two – way process between the institution 
          and the people, an intellectual intervention in the community's living problems which need to be overcome through an educational 
          process. Extension is a perfect blend of theory with practice.</p>

          <p>It will orient the students with the skills required in community development and would sensitize them towards various issues 
          of these marginalized groups and instill enough confidence and satisfaction for taking up the cause of the development of those groups.</p>

          <p>As the name of the programme itself – BEMBALA suggests, it aims to reach out the deprived groups and vulnerable sections of society and 
          create opportunities for education , awareness and skill enhancement. It intend to create a learning process for faculty and students through 
          exposure to comminity needs, problems, and issues. It hopes to reach out to the community by designing need based interventions and generating research.</p>

          <p>Eventually it will facilitate networking and linkages of the community with NGOs, institutions, and government agencies for the effective service 
          delivery and advocacy support. It also hopes to link up with the corporate sector within the parameters of Corporate Social Responsibilities ( CSR )</p> 
        </div>

      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="my-3">
        <img src="images/outreach.webp"  alt="outreach" class="img-fluid rounded-4" loading="lazy" itemprop="image">

         It regularly subscribes best and top national and international journals, periodicals/magazines and daily newspapers. 
         It caters to the needs of more than 9000 undergraduate, postgraduate and research-level staff and students. 
         The library is fully automated; it has two spacious reading halls and can accommodate two hundred and fifty users at any time. 
         The library operations are managed by the latest version of Koha Integrated Library Management System Software, and the digital 
         library using DSpace software for digital library and institutional repository. The library is upgraded with barcode and Radio 
         Frequency IDentification (RFID) technology. The library is well equipped with all the modern facilities and resources 
         (print and electronic) in the form of CDROMs, DVD-ROM, video cassettes, books, journals, etc. The library follows 
         the Dewey Decimal Scheme of classification, AACR-II cataloguing code, and MARC-21 format for bibliographic data. 
         Books are arranged on the shelves in numerical order from 000-999.
        </p>
      </div>

    </div>
  </div>
</section>

            <img src="images/ncc.webp" alt="National Cadet Corps" class="img-fluid rounded-4" loading="lazy" itemprop="image">
            <div class="title-area pb-2 mt-4">
                <h2 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">
                   National Cadet Corps
                </h2>
            </div>
            
            <p>SJU has two of the oldest NCC Units of Bengaluru. The Air Wing and the Armoured Wing were started in 1954 and 1962 respectively. 
            It enrols both boys (Senior Division) and girls (Senior Wing). The cadets are trained by senior NCC Officers who are also faculty members of the University. 
            The enrolment in the NCC is always done keeping in mind the available vacancies.</p>

            <p>The cadets are trained in handling different weapons, and take part in flying, aero-modelling, firing, trekking, rock climbing, mountaineering, 
            cycling, Republic Day camp, and youth exchange programmes, apart from team building exercises.</p>

            <p>The cadets have received several commendations and awards for their outstanding performance. Many cadets complete the ‘C' certificate and get a direct entry to join the Armed forces.</p>

            <p>Ever since 1948 when the National Cadet Corps was created, its purpose was to create dynamic, young, bright citizens who would play an 
            important role in the country's future. The motto of NCC is “UNITY AND DISCIPLINE”. The aim of NCC is to inculcate qualities of a true leader: 
            positive thinking, right attitude, social concern and dignity. The uniform that a cadet wears ensures self-respect, discipline and obedience. 
            Every cadet undergoes meticulous training in order to shape a cadet as a productive citizen of the nation. Being an NCC cadet is not just a task, 
            but also an adventure of one's lifetime. In search of the best of men and women, tests are conducted. Students are chosen after successful completion of these tests. </p>

            <p>According to the NCC timetable, it is mandatory to conduct 20 parades in the first year. The regular parades are conducted under the watchful eyes of ANO. 
            The first few parades are focused on shaping a cadet. As the saying goes “A little pressure converts a lump of coal into diamonds”. 
            Every cadet undergoes rigorous training programmes in order to be transformed into diamonds.</p>

            <p>Besides regular parades, theory classes are also held so that a cadet would be familiarised with aeroplanes, rifles and so on.</p>
        </article>

        <article class="mb-5"> 
            <div class="title-area pb-2 mt-4">
                <h2 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">
                   National Service Scheme (N.S.S)
                </h2>
            </div>
            
            <p>The National Service Scheme (NSS) is an Indian government-sponsored public service program conducted by the Ministry 
            of Youth Affairs and Sports of the Government of India. Popularly known as NSS, the scheme was launched in Gandhiji's Centenary year in 1969. </p>

            <p>St Joseph's University has been continuously in NSS since its inception with the major aim of providing opportunities to the students to 
            involve themselves in social activities and ultimately developing their personality. It is also known to have one of the oldest NSS units in 
            Karnataka State, has completed 50 years, reflecting the essence of democratic living and upholding the need for selfless service empowering 
            youth and promote national integration.</p>

            <p>Service of faith and promotion of justice is a significant component of Jesuit education across the globe. It is imperative that our 
            education need to make our students have a deep and profound faith in themselves, in each other and the divine, which needs to be realized 
            in the promotion of justice for all, especially the last, the least, and the lost who are on the periphery of society. Ultimately we need to 
            prepare students who serve the nation with resolute devotion and single-minded commitment.</p>

            <p>National Service Scheme is a voluntary organization of young students that provides services to society without bias. It aims to doctrine 
            social welfare in students through community services. Students are the building blocks of society. It is a proven fact that organized group 
            activities are potential enabling factors for cognitive developments and enriching the spirit of brotherhood. We at NSS, strive to achieve 
            similar goals through activities which have a direct impact on the society and environment at large</p>
        </article>

              </div>
              <h6>The NSS units organize the regular activities as detailed below</h6>
              <ol>
                  <li class="pb-2">General orientation of NSS Volunteers, NSS Day Celebration – 20 hrs.</li>
                  <li class="pb-2">Career guidance for the NSS volunteers – 30 hrs.</li>
                  <li class="pb-2">Community Work including Campus work and one-day camp – 70 hrs.</li>
              </ol>
            </div>

              <p>Special Camping forms an integral part of National Service Scheme. 
              It has special appeal to the youth as it provides unique opportunities 
              to the students for group living, collective experience sharing and constant interaction with community.</p>

                        <h2 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">NSS Programme Coordinator Message</h2>
                    </div>
                    
                    <p class="lead" style="font-style: italic; color: #555; border-left: 4px solid #ffc107; padding-left: 15px;">
                        "It gives me immense pride and satisfaction to reflect on the remarkable journey of our NSS volunteers at St Joseph's University."
                    </p>

                    <p>Over the years, this program stands as a true testament to the dedication, leadership, and unwavering commitment of our students towards community service and nation-building. Our volunteers have consistently brought laurels to the institution through participation in prestigious platforms like National Integration Camps fostering cultural exchange and unity in diversity, State Youth Festivals showcasing talents and team spirit, inter-college competitions securing overall winner positions across diverse fields, and special honors such as representing the Karnataka contingent in the State Republic Day parade.</p>

                    <p>Since the National Service Scheme's inception in 1969—with our unit proudly celebrating its Golden Jubilee in 2019—we have embodied the motto <strong>“Not Me, But You,”</strong> empowering youth through hands-on service that promotes social welfare, awareness, and mutual respect.</p> 

                    <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4 mb-3">Key Initiatives</h5>
                    <ul class="mb-4">
                        <li class="pb-2">Blood donation camps addressing shortages in government hospitals.</li>
                        <li class="pb-2">First aid workshops, mental health sessions, and personality development programs for life-saving skills and well-being.</li>
                        <li class="pb-2">Cleanliness drives, World Environment Day celebrations, and sustainability efforts for hygiene and environmental health.</li>
                        <li class="pb-2">Road safety campaigns to reduce accidents.</li>
                        <li class="pb-2">Daily human rights observances uniting diverse groups to uphold dignity and respect.</li>
                        <li class="pb-2">NSS Exposure Camps helping volunteers grasp rural socio-economic and cultural realities while inculcating empathy and oneness.</li>
                    </ul>

                    <p>Our volunteers work tirelessly, day and night, to support the needy and elevate lives with dignity. These accomplishments reflect the collective efforts of our NSS family—dedicated volunteers, student leaders, supportive faculty, and well-wishers—building compassion, discipline, leadership, and civic responsibility. Looking ahead, I am confident this spirit will continue inspiring greater enthusiasm and societal impact.</p>
                </div>

      <main class="col-lg-9 content-area">
        <article class="mb-5 mt-4">
            <div class="title-area pb-2">
                <h2 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">Implementation of NSS Programmes <br><span class="fs-4 text-muted fw-normal">(Institution Level)</span></h2>
            </div>
            
            <div class="mb-5 mt-4">
                <div class="left_title_border mb-3">
                    <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> a. Enrolment of NSS Volunteers</h3> 
                </div>
                <div class="bg-light p-4 rounded border-start border-4 border-warning">
                    <ul class="mb-0" style="line-height: 1.8;">
                        <li>At the college level, the NSS volunteers will be enrolled from the 1st-year degree-class students.</li>
                        <li>Preference should be given to students who have worked as NSS volunteers at the +2 level.</li>
                        <li>NCC cadets will not be allowed to join NSS. Similarly, NSS volunteers will not participate in NCC or any other youth organization, except RRC, as long as they are in NSS.</li>
                        <li>This same restriction will apply to the NSS Programme Officers.</li>
                    </ul>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="mb-4">
                <div class="left_title_border mb-3">
                    <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> b. Records and Registers</h3> 
                </div>
                <p>The NSS programme is financed by public funds. Therefore, the institution should maintain the financial records and registers as required under financial rules, and these have to be kept open for inspection and audit.</p>
                <p class="mb-4">The records and registers should be properly handed over by the outgoing programme officer to the newly appointed programme officers. The following records and registers are to be maintained in the NSS units at the College level:</p>
                
                <div class="row g-4">
                    
                    <div class="col-md-6">
                        <div class="card h-100 border-0 shadow-sm">
                            <div class="card-body">
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3"><i class="bi bi-person-lines-fill text-warning fs-4 me-2 align-middle"></i> Enrolment Register</h5>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted">A register with complete particulars and profiles of the students enrolled in NSS should be maintained, unit-wise. This register should have information about the names, sex, SC/ST, and class of NSS students, their interests, and experience in NSS and other service activities.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                    <div class="col-md-6">
                        <div class="card h-100 border-0 shadow-sm">
                            <div class="card-body">
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3"><i class="bi bi-journal-check text-warning fs-4 me-2 align-middle"></i> Project Register</h5>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted">This register is to be maintained by the programme officer with the help of students. It should provide a list of the projects undertaken during the year with complete information on each project, viz; places/areas/institution, target groups, number of students (also names) involved in the particular activity and financial allotment.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                    <div class="col-md-6">
                        <div class="card h-100 border-0 shadow-sm">
                            <div class="card-body">
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3"><i class="bi bi-box-seam text-warning fs-4 me-2 align-middle"></i> Stock Register</h5>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted">A stock-register, listing separately the consumable and non-consumable items, should be maintained. In addition, an issue/lending register must be maintained for the purpose of verification and periodic stock-checking. The entries in the stock-register will be initialed or countersigned by the Head of the institution.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                    <div class="col-md-6">
                        <div class="card h-100 border-0 shadow-sm">
                            <div class="card-body">
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3"><i class="bi bi-calendar-check text-warning fs-4 me-2 align-middle"></i> Attendance Register</h5>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted">Attendance of student volunteers at the various sessions/camps of NSS must be recorded and their signatures must also be obtained.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                    <div class="col-md-6">
                        <div class="card h-100 border-0 shadow-sm">
                            <div class="card-body">
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3"><i class="bi bi-book text-warning fs-4 me-2 align-middle"></i> Minutes Book</h5>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted">The Programme Officer should record the minutes of meetings of the advisory committee and other meetings held periodically. This would help him/her in taking suitable follow-up action.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                    <div class="col-md-6">
                        <div class="card h-100 border-0 shadow-sm">
                            <div class="card-body">
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3"><i class="bi bi-journal-text text-warning fs-4 me-2 align-middle"></i> Personal Space Work-Dairy</h5>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted">Maintaining a personal work-diary will be useful for the programme officer wherein he/she notes the project details, difficulties encountered in the project, the number of hours spent for NSS, and future plans of action.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                    <div class="col-12">
                        <div class="card h-100 border-0 shadow-sm bg-light">
                            <div class="card-body p-4">
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3"><i class="bi bi-bank text-warning fs-4 me-2 align-middle"></i> Financial Records</h5>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted mb-3">While the college office is responsible for separately maintaining accounts for NSS ensuring their audit, the programme officer concerned should keep himself/herself informed of the progress of the expenditure and be aware of the accounting procedure adopted by the institution office. He/she would ensure submission of expenditure statement and utilization certification to the university/state government in time.</p>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted mb-3">Colleges having more than one NSS unit may select one of the programme officers to look after the accounts, records, reports, and returns etc. The accounts regarding the receipt of NSS grants and their utilization will be maintained as per financial norms. These accounts will be open for inspection to audit parties, officers of NSS organization, State Liaison Officer, and Programme Coordinator also. NSS accounts will be maintained separately and will not be integrated with other accounts of the institution.</p>
                                <p class="card-text text-muted mb-0">The programme officers will send periodical reports to the NSS programme coordinator on the prescribed proforma. Copies of such reports will be endorsed to the NSS Regional Centre and State Liaison Officer. Reports of special camping projects undertaken by the NSS units may also be sent to the programme coordinator, under intimation to the NSS Regional Centre and State Liaison Officer for information and projection at an appropriate level.</p>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>

                </div>
            </div>

        </article>
      </main>

    </div>
  </div>
</section>

      <main class="col-lg-9 content-area">
        <article class="mb-5 mt-4">
            <div class="title-area pb-2">
                <h2 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">Programme Officer - Duties and Functions</h2>
            </div>
            
            <p class="lead mb-4" style="font-size: 1.1rem; color: #555;">
                The Programme Officer is expected to motivate student youth to understand the values and philosophy of N.S.S. The overall function of the programme officer is to help students plan, implement, and evaluate NSS activities and provide proper guidance and direction.
            </p>

            <p class="mb-5">To discharge their obligations, the programme officer plays multiple roles to improve the quality and magnitude of the NSS programme in the institution.</p>

            <div class="row g-4 mb-5">
                
                <div class="col-md-6">
                    <div class="card h-100 border-0 bg-light shadow-sm role-card">
                        <div class="card-body">
                            <div class="d-flex align-items-center mb-3">
                                <i class="bi bi-diagram-3 role-icon me-3"></i>
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-0">As an Organizer</h5>
                            </div>
                            <ul class="mb-0 text-muted" style="font-size: 0.95rem;">
                                <li>Interpret the scheme to students and the college community to create awareness.</li>
                                <li>Motivate, recruit, and select students for NSS work.</li>
                                <li>Enlist cooperation and coordination of community agencies, government departments, and NGOs.</li>
                                <li>Select service projects based on utility and feasibility.</li>
                            </ul>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="col-md-6">
                    <div class="card h-100 border-0 bg-light shadow-sm role-card">
                        <div class="card-body">
                            <div class="d-flex align-items-center mb-3">
                                <i class="bi bi-book role-icon me-3"></i>
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-0">As an Educator</h5>
                            </div>
                            <ul class="mb-0 text-muted" style="font-size: 0.95rem;">
                                <li>Orient volunteers by explaining the concept of social service and teaching necessary methods and skills.</li>
                                <li>Promote community education through meetings, talks, news bulletins, and discussions.</li>
                                <li>Help formulate NSS programmes that have direct relationships with the academic curricula.</li>
                            </ul>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="col-md-6">
                    <div class="card h-100 border-0 bg-light shadow-sm role-card">
                        <div class="card-body">
                            <div class="d-flex align-items-center mb-3">
                                <i class="bi bi-link-45deg role-icon me-3"></i>
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-0">As a Coordinator</h5>
                            </div>
                            <ul class="mb-0 text-muted" style="font-size: 0.95rem;">
                                <li>Coordinate NSS activities in accordance with student abilities and community demands.</li>
                                <li>Coordinate internal teaching expertise to enhance student knowledge and skills.</li>
                                <li>Coordinate external resources (government services, welfare agencies, voluntary bodies) for NSS success.</li>
                            </ul>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="col-md-6">
                    <div class="card h-100 border-0 bg-light shadow-sm role-card">
                        <div class="card-body">
                            <div class="d-flex align-items-center mb-3">
                                <i class="bi bi-eye role-icon me-3"></i>
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-0">As a Supervisor</h5>
                            </div>
                            <ul class="mb-0 text-muted" style="font-size: 0.95rem;">
                                <li>Assist students in learning how to do their jobs effectively.</li>
                                <li>Use supervisory skills to enable students to set realistic goals, view problems as challenges, and take appropriate steps to solve them.</li>
                                <li>Assist in evaluation and follow-up work.</li>
                            </ul>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="col-md-6">
                    <div class="card h-100 border-0 bg-light shadow-sm role-card">
                        <div class="card-body">
                            <div class="d-flex align-items-center mb-3">
                                <i class="bi bi-clipboard-data role-icon me-3"></i>
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-0">As an Administrator</h5>
                            </div>
                            <ul class="mb-0 text-muted" style="font-size: 0.95rem;">
                                <li>Keep the principal, advisory committee, and university programme coordinator informed.</li>
                                <li>Run day-to-day administration and attend to correspondence.</li>
                                <li>Maintain records of student participation and activities.</li>
                                <li>Prepare periodic progress reports and annual calendars.</li>
                                <li>Keep accounts and stock in prescribed forms.</li>
                            </ul>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="col-md-6">
                    <div class="card h-100 border-0 bg-light shadow-sm role-card">
                        <div class="card-body">
                            <div class="d-flex align-items-center mb-3">
                                <i class="bi bi-megaphone role-icon me-3"></i>
                                <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-0">As a Public Relation Officer</h5>
                            </div>
                            <ul class="mb-0 text-muted" style="font-size: 0.95rem;">
                                <li>Inform the community about the scheme through press reports, radio/TV programmes, pamphlets, and seminars.</li>
                                <li>Initiate IEC campaigns for image building of NSS to inspire students and the community.</li>
                            </ul>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </div>

            </div> <hr class="my-5 border-2 text-muted opacity-25">

            <div class="title-area pb-2">
                <h3 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">Selection of the Programme Officer</h3>
            </div>
            <p class="mb-4">The selection of the programme officer will be made by the principal of the institution in consultation with the programme coordinator of the University.</p>

            <div class="row g-4">
                <div class="col-12">
                    <div class="left_title_border mb-2">
                        <h4 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold fs-5"><span></span> a. Qualifications</h4> 
                    </div>
                    <div class="ps-3 border-start">
                        <ul class="mb-0 text-muted">
                            <li>Programme Officers will be selected from the members of the teaching faculty only.</li>
                            <li>NCC Officers and physical education directors should not be appointed as NSS programme officers.</li>
                            <li>In women's colleges or for a women's unit, a lady teacher should be appointed. Male members may assist the lady programme officers.</li>
                            <li>A teacher who has a high level of motivation towards community work and a good rapport with students should be preferred.</li>
                        </ul>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 mt-4">
                    <div class="left_title_border mb-2">
                        <h4 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold fs-5"><span></span> b. Tenure</h4> 
                    </div>
                    <div class="ps-3 border-start">
                        <p class="text-muted mb-0">The maximum period for which a teacher is appointed as programme officer will be 3 years in the first instance. However, this period is extendable for two more years based on a review of their performance by the principal and programme coordinator.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div class="col-12 mt-4">
                    <div class="left_title_border mb-2">
                        <h4 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold fs-5"><span></span> c. Training / Orientation</h4> 
                    </div>
                    <div class="ps-3 border-start">
                        <p class="text-muted mb-2">The programme officer will be sent for an orientation course within 3 months of selection. They must undergo the training within one year of appointment if no course is conducted in the stipulated 3-month period.</p>
                        <p class="text-muted mb-2">The principal will intimate the programme coordinator, NSS Regional Centre, and TORC/TOC regarding the selection, and ensure the officer attends the orientation. It is the head of the institution's obligation to relieve the officer for this purpose.</p>
                        <p class="text-muted mb-0">If the selected officer does not undergo orientation training for any reason within one year of selection, they will cease to function as a programme officer, and another person will be selected and trained. No programme officer will continue to work without proper orientation within the stipulated period.</p>
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>

        </article>
      </main>

    </div>
  </div>
</section>

        <p class="mt-3">SJU believes in the holistic development of students, and sports and games are integral elements of this training. 
        The Institution has played a proactive and supportive role in encouraging sports through the years, producing many great sportspersons 
        of whom many visited the campus as chief guests to flag off the sports day. The Institution is also sensitive to the special needs of sportspersons.</p>
        <p>We have facilities for sports ranging from Badminton, Athletics, Hockey, Cricket, Football, Basketball, Volleyball, Table Tennis, 
        Throwball and a number of intramural events. Indoor games, such as Chess, Carrom and Table Tennis are also played on campus. 
        We take pride in the involvement of a significant number of our students in a wide range of sports and games beyond the familiar, 
        extending into American Football, Fencing, Netball, Archery and traditional games such as Kabbadi and Kho- Kho.</p>
        <p>There are well qualified sports faculty with a Director of Physical Education, a full-time sports assistant, assisted by 
        two other staff members. Coaches for various team games are made available by the Department of Physical Education.</p>

            <!-- Guidelines List -->
            <div class="guideline-item d-flex align-items-start">
              <i class="bi bi-file-text guideline-icon"></i>
              <p><strong>Initial Screening : </strong>The committee screens submissions for compliance with basic requirements, such as format, 
              length, and relevance. Non-compliant submissions may be returned for revision or rejected.</p>
            </div> 
            
            <div class="guideline-item d-flex align-items-start">
              <i class="bi bi-file-text guideline-icon"></i>
              <p><strong>Double-Blind Peer Review :</strong> Submissions undergo a double-blind review to evaluate originality, relevance, rigor, 
              clarity, and impact. Reviewers provide comments and recommendations, which may include accepting, revising, or rejecting them.</p>
            </div>
            
            <div class="guideline-item d-flex align-items-start">
              <i class="bi bi-file-text guideline-icon"></i>
              <p><strong>Reviewer Feedback and Revisions:</strong> The committee will consolidate the feedback and authors may be asked to revise based on reviewer comments.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="guideline-item d-flex align-items-start">
              <i class="bi bi-file-text guideline-icon"></i>
              <p><strong>Final Decision:</strong> The committee will communicate the final decisions to authors regarding acceptance, 
              conditional acceptance, or rejection by January 3rd, 2025.</p>
            </div>
            
        </article>

          <div class="title-area pb-2">
                <h2 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">
                   About the <span class="text-warning">School of Chemical Sciences and the Department of Chemistry</span>
                </h2>
            </div>
             <p>The School of Chemical Sciences at St Joseph's University comprises the Department of Chemistry (established in 1927) 
             and the Department of Biochemistry (established in 2020). It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes 
             in chemistry and  undergraduate programmes in biochemistry. Known for its highly qualified faculty and carefully curated 
             syllabi, the school emphasizes analytical thinking through research-based pedagogical tools and project work, leading to 
             student publications in renowned journals.</p>

             <p>The school's research facilities include advanced scientific instruments, enabling work in catalysis, materials chemistry, 
             electrochemistry, organic synthesis and protein chemistry. The academic staff has guided over 35 Ph.Ds and, published more than 
             400 research publications in peer-reviewed journals, and received support from prestigious funding agencies. The Department has 
             earned DBT-STAR and DST-FIST recognition. It collaborates nationally and internationally with highly reputed institutions and is 
             supported by MOU with chemical industries.</p>

             <p>The undergraduate and postgraduate Chemical societies organize various activities, including lectures by prominent scientists, 
             inter-collegiate events and outreach programs. The chemistry department strives for academic excellence to develop skilled chemists 
             who contribute positively to the society.</p>
            
            
          </article>

          <div class="title-area pb-2">
                <h2 class="fw-bold mb-3 text_blue">
                   About the<span class="text-warning"> University</span>
                </h2>
            </div>
             <p>St Joseph's University (SJU) is a Jesuit university at the heart of Bengaluru, the Silicon City of India. 
             Established in 1882 by Paris Foreign Fathers, the college management was handed over to the Jesuit order 
             (Society of Jesus) in 1937. The college was first affiliated with the University of Madras and later with 
             the Mysore and Bangalore universities. In 1986, St Joseph's College became the first affiliated college in 
             Karnataka to offer postgraduate courses. In 1988, it became the first college in Karnataka to get a research 
             center, and in 2005, it was one of the five colleges in Karnataka that was awarded academic autonomy. 
             In February 2021, the St Joseph's University bill was presented in the Karnataka Legislative Assembly 
             and was subsequently passed by the Legislative Assembly and Karnataka Legislative Council. The college 
             received its University status on 2nd July 2022 and was inaugurated as India's first public-private university 
             by the Hon'ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu on 27th September 2022.</p>
            
            
          </article>

		  <div class="mt-3" >		  
			  
     
     <p>St Joseph's University in Bengaluru is a distinguished Jesuit institution with a legacy that stretches back to 1882. Located in the heart of India's vibrant Silicon City, the University embodies the Jesuit spirit of Fide et Labore, meaning Faith and Toil, blending intellectual rigor with a deep commitment to human values. Founded by the Paris Foreign Mission Society and entrusted to the Jesuits in 1937, St Joseph's has consistently been a trailblazer in higher education. It became the first affiliated college in Karnataka to offer postgraduate programmes in 1986, the first to establish a Research Centre in 1988, and one of the earliest institutions in the state to receive academic autonomy in 2005. In 2022, it attained full university status as India's first Public Private Partnership University, inaugurated by the Honourable President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu.</p>
	<p>Today, St Joseph's University offers a wide spectrum of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across the sciences, arts, commerce, and emerging fields, all within an eco friendly campus shaped by research and holistic formation. With an accomplished faculty, vibrant centres of excellence, and alumni who have excelled nationally and globally, the University nurtures leaders who are intellectually strong, socially conscious, and morally grounded. At St Joseph's, every student is valued, supported, and inspired.</p>
    
</div>

             <div class="left_title_border mb-2">
                <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>About St. Joseph's University</h3> 
             </div>
             <p>St Joseph's University is a Jesuit university at the heart of Bengaluru, the silicon city of India. 
             Established in 1882 by Paris Foreign Mission Fathers, the management of the college was handed over to 
             the Jesuit order (Society of Jesus) in 1937. In 2005, it was one of five colleges in Karnataka that was 
             awarded academic autonomy. In February 2021, St Joseph's University Bill was presented in the Karnataka 
             Legislative Assembly and was subsequently passed by the Legislative Assembly and Karnataka Legislative Councill. 
             The college received its University status on 2 July 2022 and was inaugurated as India's first Public-Private-Partnership 
             University by the Honourable President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu on 27 September 2022.</p>
            
          </article>
          <article class="pdf-viewer"> 
              
             <div class="left_title_border mt-5 mb-2">
                <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>About Our Department</h3> 
             </div>
             <p>The Department of Biotechnology at St. Joseph's University is a center of excellence in biotechnology education and research, 
             with state-of-the-art laboratories and a strong curriculum integrating lectures, practical sessions, workshops, and international 
             collaborations. Established 20 years ago, the department has received prestigious funding, including the DBT Star College Scheme 
             (2014, elevated in 2018) and VGST-CISEE grants from the Government of Karnataka. Our well-equipped labs support research in 
             microbial screening, plant phytochemistry, tissue culture, molecular markers, and bioinformatics. We emphasize target-oriented learning, 
             supported by highly accomplished faculty, ensuring students gain both theoretical and practical expertise. Our postgraduate program offers 
             an exclusive curriculum, enabling seamless progression from undergraduate to advanced biotechnology studies. With a commitment to innovation, 
             hands-on training, and career-focused education, the department nurtures future biotechnologists, preparing them for academia, research, and industry. 
             The department offers UG, PG and PhD courses in Biotechnology.</p>
            
          </article>

        <p class="mt-3">The distinctiveness of the Air Wing NCC lies in activities like microlight flying to promote airmanship, 
        where cadets receive training to fly aircraft as co-pilots. Additionally, a flight simulator is set up to help cadets improve their flying skills.</p>

        <p>The program also includes skeet shooting, which is also an international sport where a moving target is shot with a shotgun, and 0.22 firing to develop cadets' marksmanship.</p>

        <p>Aeromodelling, even though considered one of the costliest hobbies, is part of the training curriculum where in cadets are 
        trained to construct aircraft models- Radio controlled, Control line and Static, to instil values of craftsmanship in cadets.</p>

        <p>Drill instils discipline, confidence, comradeship, and physical strength in cadets. Additionally, tent pitching is also a 
        fascinating activity that promotes time management and team coordination in cadets.</p>

                 <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> Introduction to YRC</h3> 
          </div>
          
          <div class="row align-items-center mb-4">
              <div class="col-md-8">
                  <p class="content-text">The <strong>Youth Red Cross (YRC)</strong> is the student wing of the Indian Red Cross Society, which is a voluntary humanitarian organization working across India. The origin of this movement goes back to 1863, when the global Red Cross Movement was founded, now known as the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, with the aim of reducing human suffering and promoting peace across countries. In India, the Indian Red Cross Society was established in 1920 under the Indian Red Cross Society Act.</p> 
                  <p class="content-text">The Youth Red Cross (YRC) was later introduced in India as a student wing to involve young people in humanitarian and social service activities. In Karnataka, the Youth Red Cross (YRC) was formally introduced and strengthened in educational institutions around the early 2000s under the guidance of the state branch in Bengaluru and the Department of Higher Education, Government of Karnataka.</p>
              </div>
              
              <div class="col-md-4 text-center mt-4 mt-md-0">
                  <div class="logo-box">
                      <img src="https://sjudata.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/yrc/461777642_893473595535402_2233801136692289964_n.jpg" alt="YRC Logo" class="img-fluid">
                  </div>
                  <h6 class="fw-bold text_blue">Indian Red Cross Society</h6>
                  <small class="text-muted">SJU Student Wing</small>
              </div>
          </div>

          <div class="bg-light p-4 rounded-4 shadow-sm mb-4 border-start border-warning border-4">
              <h5 class="fw-bold text_blue mb-3">What the YRC Symbol Means</h5>
              <p class="content-text mb-0">The symbol of the Red Cross is a red cross on a white background, which is recognized worldwide as a sign of care, protection, and neutrality. The red colour represents sacrifice and courage, while the white background stands for peace and equality. This symbol is used in hospitals, disaster areas, and emergency services to show that help is being provided. It also reminds volunteers to serve everyone equally without discrimination and to follow humanitarian values.</p>
          </div>
          
          <hr class="my-5 opacity-25">
          
          <div class="row align-items-center">

                        <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> SJU Unit Affiliation</h3> 
                 </div>
                <p class="content-text">In Karnataka, YRC functions under the State Branch in Bengaluru, following the guidelines of the Government of Karnataka, Department of Higher Education. The affiliation of a YRC unit means that the institution is officially recognized to conduct activities such as first aid training, blood donation drives, awareness campaigns, and disaster management programmes.</p>

                      <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> Motto and Symbol</h3> 
               </div>
              <p class="fs-6 text-muted">The motto of the Youth Red Cross is <strong>“Service to Humanity,”</strong> which reflects the idea of helping people selflessly without expecting anything in return. It encourages students to develop kindness, empathy, and a sense of social responsibility.</p> 
              <p class="fs-6 text-muted">The symbol of the Red Cross is a red cross on a white background, which is recognized worldwide as a sign of care, protection, and neutrality. The red colour represents sacrifice and courage, while the white background stands for peace and equality.</p>
          </div>

          <hr class="my-5 opacity-25">

          <div> 
               <div class="left_title_border mt-5 mb-2">
                      <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> Objectives of YRC</h3> 
               </div>
               <ul class="mt-3 text-muted fs-6" style="line-height: 1.8;">
                  <li>Develop humanitarian values and social responsibility among students.</li>
                  <li>Promote awareness about health, hygiene, and sanitation, especially in rural and underprivileged areas.</li>
                  <li>Provide training in first aid and emergency response for accidents and disasters.</li>
                  <li>Build leadership qualities, teamwork, and discipline.</li>
                  <li>Encourage participation in social service activities.</li>
                  <li>Spread awareness about blood donation.</li>
                  <li>Promote environmental protection and sustainability.</li>
                  <li>Create awareness about disease prevention.</li>
                  <li>Foster unity and understanding among people from different backgrounds.</li>
                  <li>Help students gain confidence, practical knowledge, and a strong sense of responsibility towards society.</li>
               </ul>
          </div>

          <hr class="my-5 opacity-25">

          <div> 
               <div class="left_title_border mt-5 mb-2">
                      <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span> Student Volunteer Guidelines</h3> 
               </div>
              <p class="fs-6 text-muted">Student volunteers must follow discipline and actively participate in all YRC activities, programmes, and camps. Attendance is important and often mandatory for completing YRC hours. Volunteers should be punctual and follow instructions given by coordinators.</p>
              <p class="fs-6 text-muted">Wearing identification badges during programmes is necessary. Volunteers should represent the organization positively and maintain good conduct. Discrimination based on caste, religion, or gender is strictly not allowed. All members must follow the principles of humanity, neutrality, and service. Teamwork, cooperation, and a helpful attitude are very important qualities expected from every volunteer.</p>
          </div>
           
        </section>
      </div>

  <div class="container"> 
  <div class="verify-card p-5" style="background: #f8f9fa; border-radius: 10px;"> 
    <h3 class="section-title text_blue fw-bold mb-4"> CATEGORIES OF STUDENTS</h3> 

    <div class="terms-card">
        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">Domicile of Karnataka</h5>
        <p class="mb-3">Refers to a resident of Karnataka for the last 7 years continuously (Resident Indian Nationals who studied in the State of Karnataka for the last 7 years in a recognised school/institution).</p>

        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">Non-Karnataka Students</h5>
        <p class="mb-3">Refers to Indian Nationals who are residents of other states and or pursued their education in states other than Karnataka State excluding NRI,OCI/PIO & Foriegn Nationals.</p>

        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">Non-Resident Indian (NRI)</h5>
        <p class="mb-2">Refers to Indian Nationals having Indian Passports and studied/studying abroad. They must have had 3 (Three) years of education in any foreign country during the last 6 (six) years and must have passed the qualifying examination or equivalent from abroad.</p>
        <p class="mb-2">A candidate who falls under any of the following classifications shall apply under the NRI student category:</p>
        <ul class="mb-3">
            <li>NRI as defined under the Indian Income Tax Law.</li>
            <li>Either of the parents is outside India on a work permit/resident permit.</li>
            <li>Indian citizen financed by any institution/agency outside India, even if parents are residents of India.</li>
        </ul>
        <p class="mb-3">Candidates who have completed their last qualifying examinations outside India (even if affiliated with CBSE or any other board or university within India) shall apply under the NRI category.</p>

        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)</h5>
        <p class="mb-2">Refers to a Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) having an international passport and OCI card issued by the concerned Indian Mission whose parents and or grandparents are of Indian Origin.</p>
        <p class="mb-2">An Overseas Citizen of India (OCI):</p>
        <ul class="mb-2">
            <li>whose parents/grandparents were a citizen of India at the time of, or at any time after 26 <sup>th</sup> January 1950; or</li>
            <li>whose  parents/grandparents were eligible to become a citizen of India on 26 <sup>th</sup> January 1950; or</li>
            <li>whose  parents/grandparents belonged to a territory that became part of India after 15 <sup>th</sup> August 1947; or</li>
            <li>who is a child or a grandchild or a great-grandchild of such a citizen; or</li>
            <li>who is a minor child of such persons mentioned above; or</li>
            <li>who is a minor child and whose both parents are citizens of India or one of the parents is a citizen of India - is eligible for registration as an OCI cardholder.</li>
        </ul>
        <p class="mb-2">Besides, a spouse of foreign origin of a citizen of India or spouse of foreign origin of an Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder and whose marriage has been registered and subsisted for a continuous period of not less than two years immediately preceding the presentation of the application is also eligible for registration as OCI cardholder.</p>
        <p class="mb-2">However, no person, who or either of whose parents or grandparents or great grandparents is or had been a citizen of Pakistan, Bangladesh or such other country as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify, shall be eligible for registration as an Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder.</p>
       <!-- <p class="mb-3"><strong>Note:</strong> 'ordinarily resident' will mean a person staying in a particular country or India for a continuous period of 6 months.</p> -->

        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">Person of Indian Origin (PIO)</h5>
        <p class="mb-2">Refers to a foreign citizen having an international passport with a PIO card issued by the concerned Mission, who held an Indian Passport at any point in time or whose parents/grandparents were citizens of India.</p>
        <p class="mb-2">Every person of Indian origin who is a citizen of another country, NOT being a citizen of any country that may be specified by the Government of India from time to time, will be eligible to apply for a PIO Card if:</p>
        <ul class="mb-2">
            <li>the person at any time held an Indian passport, or</li>
            <li>the person or either of his/her parents or grandparents or great grandparents was born in and was permanently resident in India, provided further that neither was at any time a citizen of any of the aforesaid excluded countries; or</li>
            <li>the person is the spouse of a citizen of India or a person of Indian origin covered under (i) or (ii) above.</li>
        </ul>
        <p class="mb-2">Presently, the specified countries whose nationals are ineligible for grant of PIO Card are Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Afghanistan, Iran, China and Nepal. Further, if the applicant himself or either of his parents, grandparents or great-grandparents held the nationality of these specified countries at any time, he will not be granted a PIO Card.</p>
     <!--   <p class="mb-3">Iranian nationals of Indian origin can be considered for grant of PIO card. The Missions or other agencies authorised to issue PIO cards would obtain prior clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs before issuing the card to an Iranian national.</p> -->

        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">SAARC Nationals</h5>
        <p class="mb-3">Refers to Foreign Nationals of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.</p>

        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">Foreign Nationals</h5>
        <p class="mb-2">Refers to all Foreign Nationals except SAARC Nationals and OCI and PIO card holders. Applicants to undergraduate/postgraduate programmes who have studied abroad or applicants who are foreign nationals should meet the following criteria:</p>
        <ul class="mb-3">
            <li>Students who have studied International Curriculum must obtain an equivalence certificate from the University Grants Commission (New Delhi). <a href="https://www.ugc.ac.in/equivalence" target="_blank">https://www.ugc.ac.in/equivalence</a></li>
            <li>Applicants pursuing an IB curriculum must have 3 HL and 3 SL with 24 credits.(IB Diploma)</li>
            <li>Applicants pursuing GCE / Edexcel must have a minimum of 3 A levels with a grade not less than C.</li>
        </ul>

        <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">English Proficiency</h5>
        <p class="mb-2">Proof of English Proficiency is essential for a candidate who has not studied at an Institution located in an English-speaking country. School/College education should have had the English language as a medium of instruction. Such a candidate has to provide one of the following two scores. The validity of the test should be two years from the date of examination.</p>
        <ul class="mb-0">
            <li><strong>International English Language Testing System (IELTS)</strong>-Academic version- minimum score of 6.0 is required.</li>
            <li><strong>Test of English as Foreign Language (TOEFL)</strong>
                <ul>
                    <li>Paper-based TOEFL: a minimum score of 500 is required.</li>
                    <li>Computer-based TOEFL: a minimum score of 175 is required.</li>
                    <li>Internet-based TOEFL: a minimum score of 60 is required.</li>
                </ul>
            </li>
        </ul>
                <h5 class="text_blue fw-bold mt-4">Note:</h5>
<p class="mb-2">For more details Please visit our website: <a href="https://www.sju.edu.in/internationalstudents/admissionguidelinesforinternationalstudents" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-primary text-decoration-underline">Admission Guidelines</a></p>

    </div>
   </div> 
 </div>
</section>

	<p> The main objectives of the Anti-ragging committee, which is one of the statutory   Committees of the University, are as follows: </p>
	  <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Eliminate ragging in all its forms in the University.</li>
<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Create awareness amongst the students of what constitutes ragging.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Prevent the occurrence of ragging.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Give publicity of the measures initiated for curbing the menace of ragging.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Initiate punitive action as per the UGC guidelines, on those who indulge in ragging after a thorough enquiry. </li> 
                     </ul>

           <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>Introduction</h3> 
				
			<div class="mb-3">“AICUF (All India Catholic University Federation) is a movement of university student with a vision for a new and just society. Progressing in a history of constant re-discovery and re- creation. AICUF ever tries to link itself to the emerging needs and realities of the university, the church and the wider society”</div>

		<h2>Objectives</h2>	
			
         <p>
           <ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>To help students evolve spirituality that has humanization as its core, through involvement and reflection.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>To motivate students to become involved in studies, research and activities within the university.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>To enable Christian students to play a prophetic role in their communities through a critical understanding of their faith, drawing inspiration from the Gospels, the Eucharist and their prayer life</li>
              </ul>
         </p>
		  <h3>Origin and History of The AICUF Association</h3>
          <p>All India Catholic University Federation is a movement of university students with a vision for a new and just society.</p>
<ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Fr. Carty SJ is the Founder of AICUF 1924</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Catholic Young Man Guild (CYMG) and Its humble Commencing at St.Joseph's College, Trichy.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Fr. Carty, S. J. guided this CYMG</li>
	<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>A Magazine ‘The Rally' was started.</li>
              </ul>
