	<h2>Change in Functioning Style in New Millennium</h2>
			
         <p>
           <ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>During this period -More Collaboration with Global International Movements & Bodies with similar ideologies and Principles</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>AICUFers took part in programmes organised by IMCS,(International Movement For Catholic Students), SAPI (South Asian People's Initiatives), WSF (World Social Forum), WYD (World Youth Day) and so on</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>National Councils, Summer Camps and Commission Programmes were given importance.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Student Centrality was stressed as always which was and is the core of AICUF movement.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Student issues and common social issues were discussed & deliberated critically But there seems to be hesitancy in plunging into action as the socio-economic-political scenario kept changing.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Training Programmes reduced......Financial Constraints came in.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>National councils in AICUF is the time to review the Unit, Regional, State, and National level AICUF programs and activities, to introspect and clarify from each other about the movement, to evaluate the activities in the light of clarity of the option and relevance of the context.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Every year new members join the council and bring newness and freshness.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>The new leaders come to listen, share views, analyse, deliberate and decide for the Federation, ratifying important steps of the states, reinforcing the constitution and meaningful traditions and experiments.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>National Councils are held every year from the 12th to the 15th of August .</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Only exception is when there is mid-term Consultation or Convention coming the dates may differ otherwise more or less the dates are fixed.Covid changed our normal life and the programmes.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>We are trying to revive our normalcy in AICUF in this new normal.</li>
			   
              </ul> </p>	
		<h4>Training Programmes conducted</h4>
		 <ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Training Programmes for the Advisors and Animators</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Training Workshops for AICUF Full –Timers</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Understanding AICUF Constitution through in-depth-study and awareness sessions for AICUFers.</li>

		<h4>Regular Events conducted in AICUF</h4>
	  <ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Leadership Development Program: </b>
AICUF mainly focuses on certain area of leadership development for students such asdalit politics, communism, fight for marginalized people, women empowerment, transgender empowerment, road safety, awareness on flood safety and role of youth in politics.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Orphanage visit: </b>
Aicuf takes initiative of insisting social responsibility in the Students. One way in which this is done by arranging regular visit to ashrams, Homes and orphanages encouraging the students to interact regularly with Residents and carrying out various activities and having interactive sessions with them.</li>
			   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Rural camps:</b>
The main objective of conducting rural camps areto create a platform for the students to understand and analyze the Rural Social System, Strategies used by the Non-Governmental Agencies, Nature of Government Intervention for the development of poor people, and to facilitate students experiences of group living.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Essay and drawing competition:</b>
This is one form of expressing by the students on a current social issue or problem to get the creative ideas and the thought of students to give a platform to express.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Awareness program:</b>
To increase the knowledge of the students on various current social issues and many other informative sessions to the students.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Rallies:</b>
Students are encouraged to go on rallies to support a social causein order to show support and spread awareness.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Stationary drive:</b>
Collect stationary from the students and donate it to the orphanage kids who are not able to afford them.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Regular meetings with Aicufer's:</b>
The main objective of this meeting is to let the Aicufer's know what is going in the council and future plans.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i><b>Camps:</b>
Here the state organises camps so all the units in the state come together to learn and get to know each other. Help the students in team building and exposure to other places.</li>
			 
		</ul>

The AICUF is affiliated to PAX ROMANA – the International Movement of Catholic Students (IMCS).  It was represented Maharashtra and India at several national and international level programs for university students, including the International Council of the IMCS.</li>

The annual YES (Youth Encounter Sessions) camps are an opportunity for personality development and socio-cultural awareness. Tutoring underprivileged children and conducting workshops for them are part of social outreach. Besides these regular annual activities, there are many other activities that the AICUF organizes for students. We look forward to being of continual service to the college and to society, especially to those who are marginalized and discriminated against.</li>

The AICUF aims to respond to various social and societal issues, especially those where inequality and injustice are rampant. Social justice and reconciliation is the basis of all AICUF activities.                       <h2>Campus Ministry</h2>
                       <p>
                        <!--
                       The Campus Ministry at St Joseph's University is a vibrant team of teaching faculty who take care of the corporal and spiritual needs of students and staff members. At the spiritual level, Holy mass is organised every Friday with special emphasis on first Friday masses. Four special masses are celebrated for the inauguration of the academic year, the feasts of St Joseph, St Ignatius of Loyola and Christmas. The Campus Ministry organizes HRD classes for non-Catholic students and theology classes for second-semester Catholic students. All India Catholic University Federation (AICUF), under the guidance of the Campus Ministry, has its own coordinators and is involved in organising masses, as well as various outreach programmes, organizing MAGIS, and attending workshops and conferences. A group consisting of all religious faculty and students from various congregations in the University named 'SJU Religious' also comes under the auspices of the ministry. The group helps in organising masses and talks. They pray together, have adoration, recite the rosary and conduct spiritual exercises. The Campus Ministry also takes care of the mid-day meal scheme. 
                      --> 
                      The Campus Ministry at St. Joseph's University, led by lay faculty and a Jesuit spiritual advisor, nurtures the spiritual, moral, and social development of students and staff. Rooted in Ignatian spirituality, the ministry seeks to address the holistic needs of the university community by fostering faith formation, promoting justice, and encouraging service-oriented leadership.</p>

                     <p> Through its various initiatives, the Campus Ministry attends to both the corporal and spiritual needs of the university community. At the spiritual level, Holy Mass is organised every Friday, with special emphasis on First Friday Masses. Special Masses are celebrated for the inauguration of the academic year, as well as on the feasts of St. Joseph, St. Ignatius of Loyola, Christmas, and Ash Wednesday. The ministry also facilitates Lenten services, confessions, and an annual one-day retreat for Catholic students.</p>

                     <p>The Campus Ministry organizes HRD classes for non-Catholic students and theology classes for second-semester Catholic students, fostering inclusivity and holistic formation. It also oversees the midday meal scheme as part of its outreach initiatives.</p>

                     <p>The All India Catholic University Federation (AICUF), functioning under the guidance of the Campus Ministry, is actively involved in organizing Masses, outreach programs, and MAGIS initiatives and participating in workshops and conferences.</p>

                   <p> A group called “SJU Religious,” consisting of religious faculty and students from various congregations, also functions under the ministry and contributes to organizing spiritual activities such as adoration, rosary, and retreats.</p>

                    <p>The units under the Campus Ministry include AICUF, CSA (Christian Student Association), Jesus Youth, and Ignitors (until 2025). The ministry also organizes Christmas celebrations for students and staff, including Christmas Mass.</p>
                  
                    <h4>Campus Ministry Team</h4>

                    <P>The Campus Ministry functions through a dedicated team comprising primarily lay collaborators, with one Jesuit serving as spiritual advisor, who coordinate various spiritual, formative, and outreach activities across the university. Student involvement is ensured through structured student bodies such as CSA, AICUF, and Jesus Youth, each having its own elected student council, fostering leadership and ownership among students.</P>

		<p>We are pleased to inform you that the IGNITORS- INTEGRAL FORMATION PROGRAMME  (incorporating the NEP with one credit) was successfully organized for the students of St. Joseph's University, Bengaluru by Campus Ministry till the year 2025. </p>
 <p>According to the implementation draft of the NEP 2021, each student is required to earn one credit every semester under the Skill Enhancement Category. Therefore, the KJES Youth Works organized the program in collaboration with the Campus Ministry of SJU.</p>		
   <p>“IGNITORS” commended as a fire that enkindles other fires in the world today has helped form men and women for and with others. Attending the Ignitors program aids students towards novel learning and broaden ones thought perception. Central to which is the facilitation and interaction provided by professional trainers. This is a program aimed at turning the gaze towards the betterment of society. As a result, our university endeavors to; transform the individual though holistic education which is humane and community centered. Besides, it fosters networks to promote peace, unity, and love in the societies they live in. Additionally it has helped participants to discover their momentum, uniqueness, and guiding principles in life.</p>	
				  
		<p>As a result, the growing consciousness among youngsters that they are ambassadors of justice, equity and change has brought them close towards understanding the notions of human development.</p>
		  <p>Ignitors seek to inspire students to think critically and creatively, and to cultivate their passions for committed and constructive action. The program also aims to encourage young people to dream of a better world and pursue their missions accordingly. The sessions at St. Joseph's University were successful, thanks to the systematic organization of the program and the absence of major glitches. Ignitors 2023 achieved its motto of "A Fire that Kindles other Fires" and uniquely enhanced the students' intellectual and moral development. The involvement of diverse resource persons contributed to the quality of the program. The team was composed of dynamic individuals with expertise in various fields. The sessions covered topics such as Conflict Management and Decision Making, Creative and Critical Thinking, Love and Infatuation, Stress Management and Self-care, and Career Guidance. Various in-class and extracurricular activities gave students a fun learning experience. The program aided students in the formation of their emotional, social, and faith dimensions of life, with the ultimate goal of building a genuine democratic and secular society in India. The feedback received from students was overwhelmingly positive. Ignitors has been a fascinating and challenging experience for the youth in Karnataka, with its forward-looking and integral approach. It is a co-curricular experience that contributes significantly to the integral formation of young people and adds a value component to the educational process. It is a capacity-building program that can eventually lead to a movement of youth working for the betterment of society. IGNITOR is a promising program for the present and the future.</p>
		  <p>The Integral Formation Program was recently held at St. Joseph's University with the aim of shaping the minds of the students for a better world. The program was organized by the Ignitors Committee in collaboration with St. Joseph's University Campus Ministry and Bembala Outreach Team.</p>
		  <p>This year, it ran from January 16th to January 24th, 2023. The sessions were conducted for all students across all three shifts, with 70 volunteer resource persons leading 6 sessions each for the students over the two-day period. The sessions focused on various life-motivating topics and were well received by the students, who were left feeling motivated and happy by the end of the programme.</p>
		  <p>Programs undertaken are as follows </p>

			<div class="left_title_border mt-4 mb-5">
           <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>Introduction</h3> 
				
			<div class="mb-3">Jesus Youth is an international Catholic youth movement with a Charismatic Spirituality. It is an initiative of young people, filled with the Holy Spirit,trying to reach out to other young people. The strength of the movement is its special focus on a life centered on the Lord Jesus Christ; beginning with an experience of God, nourished by prayer,the Word of God,the Sacraments, fellowship, and sharing the Good News of Jesus Christ with others. Over the years, Jesus Youth has made a huge impact on different segments of people from various walks of life.</div>
        </div>
		  
	
	 		
	<h4>Origin, History - about the Association/Club</h4>	
			
   <p>In the mid 1970s the flame of the Charismatic Renewal spread to India and to Kerala, the southernmost tip of the Indian subcontinent. The wave of the Holy Spirit gave rise to several youth groups where catholic youth encountered Jesus and the Gospel in a renewed and refreshing way. Gradually these groups began to connect to each other and in 1985, these youth groups came together for a large conference. The conference was called ‘Jesus Youth 85' and the young people who attended the conference began to call themselves ‘Jesus Youth'. These young people shared their experiences to those around, and as they moved into universities, schools, workplaces and cities, they continued to spread the exciting news of Jesus - forming prayer groups and cell groups. The spirituality, approach and creativity of the young people began to spread as a lifestyle. As many among them travelled to different countries, they carried their Jesus Youth lifestyle along with them, leading to the formation of Jesus Youth groups around the world. Today Jesus Youth is present in over 25 countries around the world.
		  
		  </p>	
		<br><h4>Objectives, Vision, and Mission:</h4>
		  
		<p>Campus ministry is one of the most active and lively ministries of the Jesus Youth, having a mission to ‘touch and transform lives in the institutions of higher education'. Today it has a
strong and vibrant presence across India and in different parts of the world. Recalling the powerful exhortation of Holy Father John Paul II, “to be the saints of the new millennium”, this ministry offers youth a platform to become the saints of today, through a lifestyle of prayer and service.</p>
		  
		<br> <h4>The Relevance :</h4> 
		 
		<p>College days are the time when the hearts and minds of students raise the deepest questions on life, meaning, future, love and hope. All are searching for different answers, though often not in the right places. A vibrant, exciting and healthy Catholic Campus Ministry in the college could  help them connect the dots and not miss out on the great adventure that God has in store for them!</p>
<p>JesusYouth strives to bring Jesus to the younger generation in a language they relate with and understand. The Campus ministry continually employs vibrant, relevant and engaging means to
educate students in the Catholic faith. Facilitating universities in their search for wisdom and truth, the ministry also caters to their faculty and staff members. Therefore,the need to increase
the number of evangelisers, students and educators alike,in the“marketplace of ideas” remains high and pressing.</p>
	<br>
	  <h4>The Vision:</h4> 
	 
	 <p> ‘Transforming Education Institutions into Faith Formation Centres' The essence of a Campus ministry can be summed up as evangelisation: “Bringing the message of Christ to the academic world” (‘Empowered by the Spirit'-USCCBdocument,1). This involves bringing students to have an encounter with Jesus Christ and helping them nurture their relationship with Him. It includes, reaching out to those who are away from theChurch and to those who hunger for the truth of the Gospel.</p>
<p>Taking the lead from Pope Paul VI, there is an urgency to go to the very roots of universities to gain souls. We “must not remain on the margins of the academic community, but must accept the
call to bring the light of the Gospel to the very centre of that world”. (‘ Empowered by the Spirit', 28). </p>
<p>The Jesus Youth Campus ministry responds to this by attending to the affective dimension of campus students. By moulding them as disciples of Jesus and instilling within them a passion
for individual conversion and institutional change, the ministry aims to transform institutions of higher education into Catholic Faith Formation centres.</p>
	  <br>

		<br><h4>Unique Features or USP of the Association</h4>
		  
		  
		  Flexible, informal and constantly experimenting, the Campus ministry is uniquely organised so
as to not become an organisation, but a thriving movement at the service of the Church. Its
ministries are products of fellowship and relationships.

		<p><a href=""><strong><span style="color: #00216d"></span></strong></a></p>
 
		  
		  
		<br> <p><strong>St Joseph's University provides mid-day meals at subsidized rates in the canteen to deserving needy students who:</strong></p> 
		 <ul class="language-list mt-2 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>Belong to socially and economically deprived sections of the society</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>Travel from distant and rural places</li>
                  
              </ul> 
		  <p> Preference will be given to deserving students who are economically poor.</p>

<p> Those students who opt for shift III are provided with evening snacks under this scheme.</p>
		 <p><strong> Procedure:</strong></p>
		 <ul class="language-list mt-2 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>Applications will be available on the University website at the beginning of the academic year.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>Duly filled in applications with the signatures of the parents must be submitted to the respective coordinators with the recommendation from the Class mentors within the stipulated date which will be announced through an official notification and on the university website.</li>
                  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>A biometric coupon will be issued through an installed machine available in the canteen premises. Students are requested to generate their coupon and submit to the canteen to avail the mid-day meal.</li>
              </ul> 
		  
		  
		  <p><strong>Notes:</strong></p>
		  <ol >
                       <li class="pb-3">Students are expected to be judicious in using the facility.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3">The facility cannot be transferred to other students in any circumstances.</li>
                  <li class="pb-3">Wasting food in any manner will be viewed seriously.</li>
			  <li class="pb-3">Food served cannot be shared with other students.</li>
              </ol> 
		  
		  	 <p>Any violation of the above conditions will attract withdrawal of the facility from the student concerned. </p>

 <p>The University Canteen has made special provisions for serving midday meals. Students are expected to maintain discipline, and cleanliness enforced by the University authorities. </p>

 <p>Morning breakfast and evening snacks are served under this scheme to Sports Students. </p>

         <p>Dear Staff and Students,</p>
         <p>In today&rsquo;s modern scientific world, the field of counselling and psychotherapy has grown in prominence, we understand how critical it is to cater to the mental health concerns of individuals as we strongly value their well-being. Decades ago, psychiatric treatment was only meant for those with serious &ldquo;mental illness&rdquo;. Seeking professional help for mental health was seen as a taboo. However, today it is making inroads in all the fields of professional and personal development and working with a counsellor is recognised to be an important avenue to improve one&rsquo;s abilities to cope and manage various situations in life.</p>
         <p>Here, at SJU, we give utmost priority to promoting and facilitating mental health services, as we believe the mental health of our students and staff to be an essential requirement to serve the vision of our institution. Hence, we have a team of competent and dedicated counsellors who are trained professionals equipped to deal with a wide variety of challenges faced by the students and staff. We have ten counselling cabins strategically placed in all the blocks of the campus to provide easy accessibility to our students and staff.</p>
         <p>My vision is to see the counselling department grow and make a difference, by creating a safe space for all who come and thereby be agents of change. I sincerely request each one of you on campus to make the best use of this wonderful facility in order to live a peaceful, stress-free and harmonious life.</p>

    <!-- Section Heading -->
    <div class="title-area text-center pb-2"><h2 class="fw-bold mb-3">Equal Oppurtunity  <span class="text-warning">Cell </span></h2></div>
    <p>The Equal Opportunities Cell has been constituted to oversee the effective implementation of policies and programs for disadvantaged groups. The Cell provides guidance and counseling with respect to academic, financial, social, and other matters. The aim of this is to enhance diversity among students, teaching and non-teaching staff. The effective implementation also eliminates any chance of discrimination against individuals or groups. Students from various social backgrounds are encouraged to maintain healthy interpersonal relationships. All efforts are made to sensitize the academic community regarding the problems associated with social exclusion and to see to the fulfillment of the aspirations of the marginalized communities. Greviances if any, related to students from the weaker section of the society, are looked into and addressed.</p>
		
 <p>The Cell also works towards coordination with the Government and other agencies/organizations to mobilize academic and financial resources to provide assistance to students of the disadvantaged groups and adopt measures to ensure due share of utilization by SC/ST in admissions, recruitments (teaching and non-teaching posts).</p>
   	

<h4>EQUAL OPPORTUNITY CELL</h4>

<section class=" py-5 mt-2 px-2">
  <div class="container">
    <!-- Section Heading -->
    <div class="title-area text-center pb-2"><h2 class="fw-bold mb-3">INTERNAL COMPLAINTS COMMITTEE  <span class="text-warning">(ICC) </span></h2></div>
    
    <p class=" text-center">(Under Prevention of sexual harassment of Women at work place, POSH ACT 2013)</p> 
	  
	  <div class="container">
    <div class="row align-items-stretch">
        <div class="col-lg-6 d-flex">
            <div>
            <img src="images/SEXUAL HARASMENT POSTER_2X3 final_page-0001.jpg" width="100%"  alt=""/> </div>
        </div>
        <div class="col-lg-6 d-flex">
            <div>
            <img src="images/SEXUAL HARASMENT POSTER_2X3 final_page-0002.jpg"  width="100%" alt=""/></div>
      </div>    
    <!--Values-->
     
    </div>
  </div>
	  
	  <br> <br>
	
    <p>St Joseph's University is committed to providing a safe environment that is free of sexual harassment (SH) irrespective of gender, race, caste, creed, religion, place of origin, sexual orientation, disability or economic status. It seeks to do so by providing the necessary support, remedial and preventive action and steps to ensure that none of its members and others associated with it are subjected to sexual harassment. This includes setting up of Internal Complainta Committee (ICC) and enforcing âZero Tolerance Policy' on sexual harassment.</p>

<p><strong>It is to be noted that complaints of sexual harassment by any other gender can be addressed to âStudent Grievance Redressal Committee' of St Joseph's University. As per the POSH Act, only women can file a complaint of sexual harassment to Internal Complaints Committee.</strong></p>
	  
	  <h4>THE BACKGROUND:</h4>

<p>All workplaces in India are mandated by law to provide a safe and secure working environment free from sexual harassment for all women.</p>

<p>In a landmark judgment, Vishaka vs. the State of Rajasthan (1997)4, the Supreme Court of India created legally binding guidelines based on the right to equality and dignity accorded under the Indian Constitution as well as by the UN Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW).</p>

<p>Since, sexual harassment results in violation of the fundamental rights of a woman to equality as per Articles 14 and 15 and her right to live with dignity as mentioned under Article 21 of the Constitution, the Government of India enacted the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. The Act is an extension of the Vishaka Guidelines issued by the Supreme Court in 1997.</p>
	  
	<h4>THE POSH ACT</h4>

<p>Having raised the bar of responsibility and accountability in the Vishaka Guidelines, the Supreme Court placed an obligation on workplaces, institutions, and those in positions of responsibility, to uphold working women's fundamental right to equality and dignity at the workplace. Three key obligations were imposed on institutions to meet that standard, namely: Prohibition, Prevention, and Redressal.</p>

<p><strong>Please see the attached document on POSH ACT 2013, for more details. </strong></p> 
   <a href="images/Sexual Harassment Act 2013.pdf" target="_blank" class="btn btn-apply" aria-label="Apply for Bachelor of Commerce program"> Sexual Harassment Act 2013 â'
          </a> <br> <br>
<p>The Supreme Court defined sexual harassment as any unwelcome, sexually determined physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct. Examples included sexually suggestive remarks about women, demands for sexual Favors, and sexually offensive visuals in the workplace. The definition also covered situations where a woman could be disadvantaged in her workplace as a result of threats relating to employment decisions that could negatively affect her working life.</p>

<p>According to the University Grants Commission Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of sexual harassment (SH) of women employees and students in Higher Educational Institutions, the constitution of Internal Complaints Committee to address the issues of SH is mandatory.  </p>
	  
	<h5>INTERNAL COMPLAINTS COMMITTEE (ICC) OF ST JOSEPH'S UNIVERSITY:</h5>

 

<p><strong>In case of Physical, Verbal, or any other Sexual Harassment of women, write a mail to icc_posh@office.sju.edu.in and thereafter a written complaint addressed to ICC.</strong></p>

<h4>FUNCTIONS OF THE COMMITTEE</h4>
<p><strong>PREVENTIVE STEPS.</strong></p>
	  
	<p>It will be the endeavour of the committee: </p> 
	 <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>To facilitate a safe environment that is free of sexual harassment</li>
<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>To create awareness about sexual harassment of women among its employees and students</li>
		   
    </ul> 
	  
	<h4>REMEDIAL STEPS</h4>
	 <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>To ensure that the mechanism for registering complaints is safe, accessible, and sensitive.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>To take cognizance of complaints about sexual harassment, conduct inquiries, provide assistance and redressal to the victims, recommend penalties, and take action against the harasser, if necessary.</li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>To advise the competent authority to issue warnings or take the help of the law to stop the harasser, if the complainant consents.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>To seek medical, police, and legal intervention with the consent of the complainant.</li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>To arrange appropriate psychological, emotional, and physical supportâincluding counselling, security, and other necessary assistanceâfor the victim, if requested.</li>
    </ul> 
	  
	  
	  <h4>PROCEDURE TO BE FOLLOWED BY THE COMMITTEE</h4>
	  
	  <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The committee shall meet as and when the complaint is received by it. Complaint can be received by any member of the committee.<br>
        <strong>Conciliation:</strong> Before the ICC initiates an inquiry into the complaint, the complainant may request the ICC (in writing/email) to settle the matter between complainant and the respondent through conciliation. However no monitory settlement shall be made the basis of the conciliation. In the event a settlement has been reached and duly recorded by ICC, further inquiry shall not be conducted. In the event that the conciliation fails then the ICC will proceed to formal process of inquiry whose steps are as follows:</li>
                       
    </ul> 
	  
 <h5>Inquiry process: </h5>

	 <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
     <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The Committee may direct the complainant to prepare and submit a detailed statement of incidents if the written complaint lacks exactness and required particulars, within two (2) days from such direction or such other period that the Committee may decide. </li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i> The Committee shall direct the accused employee/student to prepare and submit a written response to the complaint/allegations within four (4) days from such direction or such other period as the Committee may decide.</li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The Committee shall conduct all proceedings by the principles of natural justice. Both parties will be given a fair and reasonable opportunity to present their case. However, if the respondent chooses not to participate in the proceedings, the Committee reserves the right to proceed ex parte. </li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The Committee shall allow both parties to produce relevant documents and witnesses to support their case. Documents produced by either party shall be affixed with that party's signature to certify the document as an original/true copy. </li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The party against whom the document/witness is produced shall be entitled to challenge/cross-examine the same. </li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i> The Committee shall record and consider the evidence produced by both parties.</li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i> Minutes of all proceedings of the Committee shall be prepared and duly signed by the members of the Committee.</li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i> The Committee shall record its findings in writing supported with reasons and shall forward the same with its recommendations, to the Vice Chancellor/Management, after the completion of the proceedings before it. In case the Committee finds that the facts discloses that the offense by the accused person is serious and of criminal in nature, this shall be specifically mentioned in the Committee's report. Further, the committee may recommend to the institution to file an FIR with the jurisdiction police.</li>
		 <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>If, in the course of the proceedings before it, the Committee is satisfied that a prima facie case of sexual harassment is made out against the accused employee(s)/student and that there is any chance of the recurrence of any such action, or that it is required to do so in the interests of justice, it may, on the request of the complainant or otherwise, disciplinary action could be initiated in the form of, 
		 <ol>
			<li>Warning</li>
			 <li>Written apology</li> 
			 <li>Bond of good behaviour</li> 
			 <li>Adverse remarks in the confidential report</li> 
			 <li> Debarring from supervisory duties</li> 
			 <li>Denial of membership of statutory bodies</li> 
			 <li>Denial of re-employment/readmission</li> 
			 <li>Stopping of increments/promotion/denying admission ticket</li> 
			 <li>Reverting, demotion</li> 
			 <li>Suspension</li> 
			 <li>Dismissal</li>
			 <li>Any other relevant mechanism</li> 
		   </ol>
		 </li>                 
    </ul>   
	  
	 <p> (i) If, at the end of the proceedings before it, the committee is convinced that, the complainant has knowingly brought false charges of sexual harassment against any person, it shall report the same in writing to the Vice Chancellor/Management, with reasons and recommendations of the action to be taken against such person.</p>

<p>(ii) If in the course of the proceedings before it, the Committee is satisfied that any person has retaliated against /victimized the complainant or any person assisting the complainant the committee shall report the same in writing, to the Vice chancellor/Management, with reasons and with recommendations of the action to be taken against such a person.</p>
	  
	<h4>ZERO TOLERANCE POLICY (ZTP) OF ST JOSEPH'S UNIVERSITY AGAINST SEXUAL HARASSMENT </h4> 
	  <ol>
			<li>We are committed to providing a safe environment for all women in the institution free from sexual harassment.</li>
		  <li>We operate under a Zero Tolerance Policy for any form of sexual harassment within the institution. All incidents are treated with utmost seriousness, and every allegation is investigated promptly and thoroughly.</li>
		  <li>Any person involved in SH will face disciplinary action, up to and including dismissal from the institution. Further, the accused can face legal actions like FIR.</li>
		  <li>All complaints of sexual harassment will be treated with confidentiality and respect.</li>
		  <li>In this institution, no one will be victimized for making a complaint of sexual harassment. However, in the event that the inquiry process finds that the complaint is malicious or false, the recommendation for a suitable punitive action will be made against the complainant.</li>
		  
    </ol>
				
			
	  
  </div>
</section>

        <p class="text-muted small">Notification Ref: SJU/RO/STU/25/2026-27 | May 20, 2026</p>
    </div>
    
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-lg-12">
            
            <h4 class="fw-bold" style="color: #004a99;">SJU Lateral Entry Admission - Overview</h4>
            <p class="mb-4">Students who have successfully completed their 1st year (I and II Semesters) UG and PG (I and II Semesters) and have the required credentials can apply for lateral entry admission at St Joseph's University for the 2nd year (III Semester) UG and PG of the Academic Year 2026-27. For extraordinary cases, lateral admission for the 3rd year (V Semester), UG will be considered.</p>

            <h4 class="fw-bold mt-4" style="color: #004a99;">SJU Lateral Entry Admission Dates</h4>
            <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Lateral Entry Admissions starts on May 21, 2026. The last date to send the duly filled application form is June 2, 2026.</li>
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Please print the Lateral Entry Admission form after filling in the required data, scan it, and send it by email to registraroffice@sju.edu.in.</li>
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>If eligible and vacancies are available, you will be called for an offline interview after June 10, 2026. Please ensure you write your email ID legibly, as the offline interview details will be sent to this email. You are expected to be present with your parents for the offline interview.</li>
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Candidates will be called for an offline interview after June 10, 2026, and if admitted, will have to pay the fees online within 48 hours.</li>
            </ul> 
    
            <h4 class="fw-bold mt-5" style="color: #004a99;">SJU Lateral Entry Eligible Criteria</h4>
            <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Candidates seeking lateral entry should have completed all the courses offered in the 1st year of UG and PG Programmes.</li>      
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>First-year UG students should have studied Language I and Language II courses.</li>
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>St Joseph's University offers standalone and three-core subjects programmes (Triple Major). In cases where the titles of the courses/papers studied by the candidate differ from those offered by the University, the candidate may be required to submit the syllabus from the institution last attended. The same will be reviewed by the Dean of the respective School for verification and further recommendations.</li>
                <li><i class="fas fa-check"></i>Applicants are advised to carefully review the syllabus of the programme they wish to apply for, along with the second language options offered by the University, before submitting their application for lateral admission to the second year.</li>      
            </ul> 

            <h6 class="sju-notice p-3 mt-4 mb-5">Incomplete forms will be rejected.</h6>

            <div class="row align-items-stretch">
                
			<h4>Placement Process</h4>
				
	  <p>All III Year Under Graduate Students and II Year Post Graduate Students are eligible to apply to be part of the Placement Process. All II Year UG and PG students are eligible to apply for the Pre-Placement Process (Training). Following are the Steps to apply for Placement Services.</p>
        <br/>
        <div class="table-responsive">
                         <table class="table table-responsive table-bordered align-middle fee-table table-col-compact">
                         <tbody>
                             <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 1</th>
                               <td>Register for the 30 Hours Skill Development Training in the College Office and collect a Receipt (note the receipt Number)</td>
                              
                             </tr>
                             <tr>
                               <th scope="row">STEP 2</th>
                               <td>Download the Placement Application Form</td>
                             
                               
                             </tr>
                             <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 3</th>
                               <td>Submit the copy of the Confirmation Sheet to the Placement Officer</td>
                             
                             </tr>
                             <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 4</th>
                               <td> Retain One Copy for yourself.</td>
                             
                             </tr>
                           </tbody>
                         </table>
              </div>
				
				<h5>Placement Season:</h5>
<p>Official Placements will begin from July until March</p>
				<br/>
				
				<h4>How does the Placement Process work?</h4>
				
        <div class="table-responsive">
                         <table class="table table-responsive table-bordered align-middle fee-table table-col-compact">
                         <tbody>
                             <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 1</th>
                               <td>HR of a company contacts College or Placement Officer contacts the company</td>
                              
                             </tr>
                             <tr>
                               <th scope="row">STEP 2</th>
                               <td>Announcement is made of a Placement Drive, JD, CTC is announced to students</td>
                             
                               
                             </tr>
                             <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 3</th>
                               <td>Placement Representative is contacted with details with regards to Date and Timing</td>
                             
                             </tr>
                             <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 4</th>
                               <td> Students are required to Sign-Up for the Placement Drive</td>
                             
                             </tr>
							 
							<tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 5</th>
                               <td>Companies Confirm the Drive with Infrastructure Details</td>
                             
                           </tr> 
							 <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 6</th>
                               <td> Students participate in the Placement Drive (Pre-Placement Talk, Test/Personal Interview)</td>
                             
                             </tr>
							 <tr class="table-light">
                               <th scope="row">STEP 7</th>
                               <td>Short-listed Candidates are announced</td>
                             
                             </tr>
							 
                           </tbody>
                         </table>
              </div>
				<br><br>
				<h5>Selection</h5>
				
				<ul class="language-list mt-2 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>Each student is allotted a maximum of ONE Offer letter only.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>You must communicate with the company only via the Placement centre ONLY</li>
					<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>List of selected students will be put up on the notice board.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>After having accepted a job offer, if you do not wish to join the company due to genuine reasons, then you must inform the Placement Office.</li>
              </ul>
                      
				<br><br>
				
				<h6><strong>Students, who want to pursue higher studies, do refrain from Placement process.</strong></h6>
				<br><br>
								
				<h5>General Advice</h5>
				<ul class="language-list mt-2 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>Remember you are representing the college; therefore you will act responsibly and not convey any negative image about the college to companies' officials.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>You must carry copies of your resume(use template provided) originals/copies of your certificates as required , passport size photographs</li>
					<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>You must wear your ID-card at all times during placement process.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i> You are expected to be punctual for the placement process. Late comers will not be allowed.</li>
					<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>You must be formally dressed during the placement process.</li>
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-arrow-right me-2"></i>The date/time/venue of the interviews will be subject to change if situation warrants, you must be alert to announcements made</li>
					<li class="pb-3">You are also requested to forward contacts if you have any, in different companies so that the Placement Office may formally invite these companies for placements. <strong>The Placement Office reserves the right to override any of the above rules if required under special circumstances.</strong></li>
                       
              </ul>

                       <header class="info-card-header">
                 
                              <h2>Introduction</h2>
                       </header>
                       <p>The Centre for Placements and Skill Development is dedicated to empowering students by enhancing their employability and career prospects. Through comprehensive training in both technical and soft skills, we equip students with the knowledge and competencies required to thrive in their chosen fields, bridging the gap between education and industry expectations.</p>
                    </div>
										
                </div>
                
			<h4>Functions</h4>
				
	  <ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Job and Internship Sourcing
		  <ul>
			<li>Identify and source job openings and internship opportunities for final-year undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) students across various schools.</li>
			 
			</ul>
		  </li>			   
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Academia-Industry Collaboration
		  <ul>
			<li>Strengthen industry-academia interaction through guest lectures, seminars, workshops, and other initiatives.</li>
			  <li>Bridge skill gaps by aligning student competencies with industry expectations.</li>
			</ul>
		  </li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Soft Skills Training
		  <ul>
			<li>Conduct soft skills training for final-year students at the beginning of the academic year.</li>
			  <li>Prepare students for placement processes, including resume building, interview skills, and professional communication.</li>
			</ul>
		  
		  </li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Recruiter Relationship Management
		  <ul>
			<li>Maintain strong relationships with existing recruiters.</li>
			  <li>Identify and engage potential recruiters through placement brochures, LinkedIn, alumni networks, and direct outreach.</li>
			</ul>
		  
		  </li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Campus Recruitment Coordination
		  <ul>
			<li>Ensure a seamless experience for recruiters visiting the campus by managing logistics, refreshments, and other requirements.</li>
			 
			</ul>
		  </li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Effective Communication
		  <ul>
			<li>Provide timely updates on placement activities to all university stakeholders, including students, faculty, and administration.</li>
			 
			</ul>
		  </li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Placement Documentation & Compliance
		  <ul>
			<li>Maintain records of all placement-related activities in accordance with NAAC and other statutory university requirements.</li>
			 
			</ul>
		  
		  </li>
		   
		</ul>

		<h4>Organizational Structure</h4>		
			<img src="images/diagram.jpg" width="575" height="559" alt=""/> 
			
			<h4>Placement Policy</h4>
			<h5>1. Eligibility and Registration</h5>
			<ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		   <li class="pb-3">Mandatory Registration: All final-year undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) students must register on the Placement page of the Linways portal.</li>
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Participation Choice
		  <ul>
			<li>Students interested in campus recruitment must select ‘YES' during registration.</li>
			 <li>Students opting out must select ‘NO' and choose a reason from the provided dropdown list for non-participation.</li>
			</ul>
		  </li>	
		</ul>
			<h5>2. Compliance Requirements</h5>	
				<ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		   
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Registered students must adhere to university placement norms, including
		  <ul>
			<li>Maintaining the required attendance percentage.</li>
			 <li>Ensuring they have no active backlogs at the time of placement.</li>
			</ul>
		  </li>	
		</ul>
				
			<h5>3. Terms and Conditions</h5>	
				<ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		   
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Single Offer Policy: Once a student secures a placement offer from any organization, they will no longer be eligible for further campus recruitment drives.</li>
					<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Documentation Requirement: Students must submit a copy of their offer letter to the Placement Office for official records.</li>	
		</ul>
		
		<h5>Placement Drive Reporting Guidelines</h5>
		<b>Students are required to:</b>
		<ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		   
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Report on time as per the schedule shared by the Placement Office. Latecomers will not be allowed to participate in the process.</li>
			<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Carry essential documents, including
		  <ul>
			<li>A hard copy of their updated CV</li>
			 <li>College identity card</li>
			</ul>
		  </li>
			<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Dress professionally: Students should be well-groomed and dressed in formal attire for the placement drive</li>	
		</ul>
		
		<h5>4. Work Commitment</h5>	
				<ul class="language-list mt-0 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
		   
		<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>Students placed through campus recruitment drives are expected to commit to a minimum employment period of one year with the respective organization</li>

    <div class="title-area  pb-2"><h4 class="fw-bold mb-3">Prevention of Caste Based Discrimination <span class="text-warning">(D.O.F.No.1-7/2011(SCT) </span></h4></div>
    
    <p >In line with the communication dated 1st March 2016, from the office of the Registrar - U.G.C regarding the prevention of caste-based discrimination, St Joseph University hereby places on record its commitment to strive towards preventing caste-based discrimination in all its academic activities.</p> 
	
	  <h4> <strong>For preventing the Caste Based Discrimination, SJU is committed to the following aspects</strong></h4>
	  
	  
	  
	  <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The University in no manner whatsoever will tolerate caste-based discrimination in the institution. All the Faculty/University Authorities are warned to desist from any act of discrimination against SC/ST students on the grounds of their social origin.</li>
<li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Anybody who experiences or comes to know of any caste based discrimination in the University are requested to immediately bring it to the notice of the authorities.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The University Authority/Faculty will not indulge in any kind of discrimination against any community or category of students.</li>
		 
                     </ul>
	  
	  
	  
	  
	  
	  
	
	  
  </div>
</section>

<section class=" py-5 mt-2  px-2">
  <div class="container">
    <!-- Section Heading -->
    <div class="title-area  pb-2"><h2 class="fw-bold mb-3">PROCEDURE AND GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS FOR   <span class="text-warning">REDRESSAL OF GRIEVANCE OF STUDENTS </span></h2></div>
    
    <p><strong>MPORTANT NOTE: The following instructions are based on the University Grants Commission (Redressal of Grievance of Students) Regulations, 2023. Please read the instructions and the regulations carefully before submitting the Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) Form.</strong> </p> 
	
	  
	
  </div>
</section>
	
	<section>
		<div class="container">
			
			<h4> <strong>PROCEDURE FOR REDRESSAL OF GRIEVANCES BY STUDENT GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL COMMITTEE (SGRC): </strong></h4>	
	  <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
            <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The SJU Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) Form is for grievances pertaining to the students enrolled in the University or applicants seeking admission to be enrolled in the University.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>A complaint/grievance from an aggrieved student relating to the Institution shall be addressed online to the Chairperson of the SGRC only through the SGRC Form.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>On receipt of the online complaint, it will be directed to the SGRC, along with its comments within 15 days of receipt of the complaint on the online portal.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The SGRC shall send its report with recommendations, if any, to the competent authority of the University and a copy thereof to the aggrieved student within 15 working days from the date of receipt of the complaint.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The SGRC, as the case may be, will fix a date for hearing the complaint, which will be communicated to the University and the aggrieved student.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>An aggrieved student may appear either in person or authorise a representative to present the case.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Any student aggrieved by the decision of the SGRC may prefer an appeal to the Ombudsperson, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of such decision.</li>
		   <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Grievances not resolved by the SGRC within the time period provided in these regulations may be referred to the Ombudsperson by the University.</li>
		  
				</ul>
	
		<div class="mt-4">
		<h4> <strong>GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS </strong></h4>	
	  <ul class="language-list mt-3 p-0" style="list-style-type:none;">
            <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Grievances should be made within a week of the matter arising. Grievances raised after these deadlines will be considered late and if you wish that the University considers them then you will need to include a valid reason and evidence of the reason for the delay. You will then be informed either that your reason for delay has been considered valid or that your complaint is out of time.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>All sections of the form should be completed, and any supporting evidence you wish for the committee to consider should be submitted at the time of the hearing.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Grievances should be described formally and appropriately within the word limit.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>If a student or the representative does not turn up to the hearing, the case will be decided in absentia.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>Appropriate action will be taken against the complainant, where a complaint is found to be false or frivolous.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The University is not responsible for any amount paid by applicants to any individuals/groups/agencies/organisations, etc outside the University promising admissions.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The Ombudsperson shall, after giving reasonable opportunities of being heard to the parties concerned on the conclusion of proceedings, pass such order, with reasons thereof, as may be deemed fit to redress the grievance and provide such relief as may be appropriate to the aggrieved student.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The institution, as well as the aggrieved student, shall be provided with copies of the order under the signature of the Ombudsperson.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The institution shall comply with the recommendations of the Ombudsperson.</li>
		  <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2"></i>The Ombudsperson may recommend appropriate action against the complainant, where a complaint is found to be false or frivolous.</li>
		  	     </ul>
	</div>
		<div class="mt-4">	
			<h4> <strong>Grievance Redressal Procedure and Form</strong></h4>			
			<a href="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSenw4izHAb_NefKcP0BK0SJVlk8PORVSKT29tdSWcWc74VqCw/viewform" target="_blank" class="btn btn-apply" aria-label="Apply for Bachelor of Commerce program">  Click here to fill the Student Grievance Redressal Form â'
          </a>			
		</div>
			
			<div class="mt-4">	
			<a href="images/4675881_Regulation_merged.pdf" target="_blank" class="btn btn-apply" aria-label="Apply for Bachelor of Commerce program">  University Grants Commission (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023 â'
          </a>		
		</div>	
			<div class="mt-5"></div>

      function resizedUrl(url, w, h) {
        return 'https://images.weserv.nl/?url=' + encodeURIComponent(url.replace(/^https?:\/\//, '')) + '&w=' + w + '&h=' + h + '&fit=cover&q=75&output=webp';

        var img = document.createElement('img');
        img.src = resizedUrl(thumbs[n], 340, 170);

        wrap.insertBefore(img, fallback);

           <h3 class="br_title text_blue fw-bold"><span></span>Message from the Vice Chancellor</h3>

		    <div class="row gy-5 mb-5">
      <!-- Image Column -->
      <div class="col-lg-5 text-center">
        <img src="images/lobo-sj.jpg" alt="Rev Dr Victor Lobo SJ" class="img-fluid saint-img" width="390"><br/><br/>
<div><strong>Rev Dr Victor Lobo SJ </strong><br>Vice - Chancellor</div>

        <div class="saint-content">
                 <p>Dear International Student,
<p>We invite you to join St. Joseph's University, Bengaluru to have brilliant higher education career journey of your life and enrich your professional talent at one of the oldest higher education institutions in India established in 1882.</p>

<p>The University is administered by the Society of Jesus (SJ), also known as the Jesuits founded by St. Ignatius of Loyola in 1540. With their headquarters in Rome, Italy, the Jesuits are actively involved with mission of providing quality education and character formation in nearly fifty countries of the world and run such reputed world class Universities like Universidad de Buenos Aires, Argentina, Pontificia Universidad Catholica de Rio de Jameiro, Brazil, St. Mary's University, Halifax, Canada, Sophia University, Tokyo-Japan, Champion Hall – Oxford University, U.K., Boston College, Massachusetts, U.S.A., Fordham University, U.S.A., Georgetown University, Washington D.C., U.S.A., Loyola University, Chicago, U.S.A., University of San Francisco, U.S.A., Sogang University, Seoul, South Korea, IQS Barcelona, Spain, Sanata Dharma University, Indonesia, etc.</p>

<p>The Jesuits came to India in 1542 under the leadership of St. Francis Xavier and established the first ever higher education institution in India – St. Paul's College, Goa the same year (which underwent several transformations). Subsequently they established a large number of schools, colleges and seminaries in Goa and also in other prominent towns and cities of India. Most of the more than 100 year old and not for profit colleges in India are presently run by the Society of Jesus like St. Joseph's, Trichy, St. Xavier's, Kolkata, St. Xavier's, Mumbai, Loyola, Chennai, St. Aloysius, Mangalore, etc.</p>

<p>Our Institution founded as St. Joseph's College in 1882 has a glorious history of high academic achievements of more than 140 years. On 2nd July 2022 the St. Joseph's College, Bangalore was elevated to the status of an University by the Government of Karnataka under the R.U.S.A. (Rashtriya Uchchatar Siksha Abhiyan) Scheme of the Government of India, Ministry of Human Resource Development, New Delhi. St. Joseph's University, Bangalore has the unique distinction as being, the only private college in India to be raised to this status of the first of its kind Public – Private Partnership (PPP) University in India!</p>

<p>On 27th September 2022, Her Excellency Smt. Draupadi Murmu, President of India, formally inaugurated the St Joseph's University in the august presence of Hon'ble Shri Thaawar Chand Gehlot, Governor of Karnataka, Hon'ble Shri Basavaraj Bommai, Chief Minister, Hon'ble Shri C. Ashwath Narayan, Minister for Higher Education of the State and Rt. Rev. Dr. Peter Machado, Archbishop of Bangalore.</p>
<p>
The Bangalore Jesuit Educational Society (Regd) has already embarked on a mission to develop the University as a centre to provide world class education at affordable cost to all deserving young people irrespective of their caste, creed, economic status or nationality keeping in mind the triple values of academic excellence, character formation and social concern.</p>

<p>Plans are afoot to augment the infrastructure facilities like library, laboratories, computer and network system, hostels and cafeterias, sports grounds and gymnasiums, auditoriums and seminar halls, astronomical observations, student health and counselling centres, placement and skills development cells, etc at the present Lal Bagh Road Campus and also to build a huge state of the art new campus to cater to all the future expansions needs of the University in a 30 acres – Mount Saint Joseph, Bannerghatta Road in next five years time from now.</p>

<p>Saint Ignatius of Loyola had a keen desire to spread education and knowledge, media of liberation for a just and equitable society. The group he founded, the Society of Jesus, has been active in the field of education throughout the world since its origin. In the world, the Jesuits are responsible for 3,897 Educational Institutions in 96 countries. The education imparted by the Jesuits aims at the integral, personal formation of youth.</p>

                       <li class="pb-3"><i class="fas fa-check me-2" aria-hidden="true"></i>After obtaining Provisional Admission letter from the University, they have to change the Student Visa in favor of St. Joseph's University at the local Foreigners Regional Registration Office, Bengaluru, before they start attending classes at St. Joseph's University.</li>
